messages.subject: troubleshooting with gam.check  and AUC/ROC
parts:
Dear distance-sampling group,

 

First of all, thanks for sharing the great work on distance-sampling.org!!!!

 

I tried to evaluate the auc and the roc from my dsm model on transects (one-time detections) bservations of marine taxa;

My data are presence/absence obervations and no covariates.

 

I used tweedie and soap film smoother and the summary of the model is:

 

Family: Tweedie(p=1.01)

Link function: log

 

Formula:

count ~ s(x, y, bs = "so", k = 15, xt = list(bnd = list(survey.area))) +

    offset(off.set)

 

Parametric coefficients:

             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)   

(Intercept) -14.95937    0.04598  -325.4   <2e-16 ***

---

Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

 

Approximate significance of smooth terms:

         edf Ref.df     F p-value   

s(x,y) 95.71    146 9.476  <2e-16 ***

---

Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

 

R-sq.(adj) =  -11.3   Deviance explained = 32.5%

-REML = 1637.8  Scale est. = 1.0303    n = 1759

 

 

But at gam.check I have:

 

Method: REML   Optimizer: outer newton

full convergence after 18 iterations.

Gradient range [-0.005208738,0.0008577222]

(score 1637.821 & scale 1.030293).

Hessian positive definite, eigenvalue range [0.0008577205,91899.35].

Model rank =  147 / 147

 

Basis dimension (k) checking results. Low p-value (k-index<1) may

indicate that k is too low, especially if edf is close to k'.

 

          k'   edf k-index p-value   

s(x,y) 146.0  95.7    0.83  <2e-16 ***

---

Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] troubleshooting with gam.check and AUC/ROC
parts:
Hi Massimo, hi listfolks,

We don't recommend using dsm with presence/absence data, this is likely
the problem here. The Tweedie distribution is used when we have counts,
but if you only have 0/1 then it will not work very well. Indeed we see
this in your gam.check() output and that the p parameter for the Tweedie
is at it's lowest value.

If you have presence/absence data I'd recommend using an approach more
suited to that data.

hope that helps,
--dave
